elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 9.1 requires performance "in accordance with the Performance Standards and, where there are no Performance Standards, in a commercially reasonable manner and with no other or higher degree of care" — a commercial-reasonableness standard expressly capped at "no other or higher degree of care", not a professional and workmanlike warranty; the redline adds no such standard.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "M&I warrants that the software used to provide the Services will conform in all material respects to its documentation..." (16.1.B alone, covering reports conforming to User Manuals, would not have sufficed).

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "at least ninety (90) days following the date such software is first used to provide the Services" — 90 days, not 12 months.
Section 9.1 obliges M&I to perform the Services in accordance with the Performance Standards throughout the term, a continuing performance obligation exceeding 90 days in duration.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Customer's remedies ... shall include, at M&I's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services..."
Inserted: "... or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Section 16.1 as rendered contains only a systems-capability rep (A), a reports/User Manuals conformity promise (B), rights/authority reps and a Millennium-compliance rep; no general compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty, and the redline adds none.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code/virus warranty appears anywhere in Section 16.1 or in the inserted language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: express software-to-documentation warranty "in all material respects ... for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the date such software is first used to provide the Services"; the pre-existing 16.1.B reports-to-User-Manuals promise would not have qualified as a software warranty.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Section 9.1: "M&I agrees to perform the Services in accordance with the Performance Standards and, where there are no Performance Standards, in a commercially reasonable manner" — an express, continuing service-performance obligation running for the whole term, i.e. well beyond 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "...shall include, at M&I's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services..." Remedy is stated as inclusive ("shall include"), so Sections 12.3 and 13 remedies survive.
Inserted: "...or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the insertion supplies the previously absent 90-day software-to-documentation warranty and the repair/replacement/refund remedy, while the services-duration element was already met by the term-long performance obligation in Section 9.1.

Preferred level fails on four elements: no professional-and-workmanlike standard (Section 9.1 caps care at "commercially reasonable ... and no other or higher degree of care"), 90 days rather than 12 months for software, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no malicious-code warranty. Correctly classified as a deviation redlined to the fallback.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, no survival tail, expense or damages boilerplate is added, the period is set at the fallback floor (90 days) rather than exceeded, and the remedy is drafted as non-exclusive so Section 12.3 and Section 13 mechanics are not displaced.

Intent preserved: the existing carve-out "EXCEPT AS SPECIFICALLY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 16.1" in 16.1.F expressly protects the new warranty from the disclaimer, so no edit to the disclaimer is needed.

Drafting fix (non-blocking): the rendered insertion carries no subsection letter. Label it "G." within Section 16.1 so that the 16.1.F carve-out and the internal cross-reference "the warranties in this Section 16.1" clearly capture it.

Drafting fix (non-blocking): the remedy sentence is anchored to "breach of the warranties in this Section 16.1" yet refers to "non-conforming ... Services", while the services performance obligation sits in Section 9.1. To make the remedy bite on service non-performance, extend the anchor to "breach of this Section 16.1 or of Section 9.1" or move the remedy sentence to a stand-alone reference to both provisions.
